title: The Iron Worm — Editor Intro
summary: Editorial opening splash: the morning after Gunnar finally recovered north from the stars, Carrie takes him and Bjorn toward a route where the sky, landmarks and horizon disappear.
settingText: Bushwick subway entrance at street level, morning
panelPlan: Full-page editorial/title splash at a normal Bushwick subway entrance. Open sky and familiar street occupy the upper portion; the stairwell drops sharply into fluorescent darkness.
Carrie is already headed toward the stairs. Bjorn and Gunnar remain at the top for one beat while commuters stream around them without concern.
The composition should visually oppose Issue 3's final clear sky: yesterday Gunnar recovered direction by looking up; today the city asks him to go down.
Do not show the train, platform, later transfer, annex, or return trip.

dialogueInline.text: This morning, Carrie needs one stamp across town.
dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION

dialogueInline.text: There is no sky down there.
dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION

directionInline: Editorial splash. Preserve day-three knowledge limits; the subway is a first encounter, not a system Gunnar or Bjorn already understands.

title: One Stamp
summary: Carrie arrives expecting a simple DTI errand; before they leave, Bjorn keeps the household anchored by leaving the apartment key with Astrid.
panelPlan: Wide: Breakfast in 5B. Astrid and the Kin remain in the apartment while Carrie stands near the door with coffee in one hand and a neat DTI folder under the other arm; she looks prepared for an easy errand.

Medium: Carrie shows Bjorn and Gunnar the single paper that needs to be carried to another DTI office; neither reads it. Gunnar asks how far; Carrie tells them the trip requires the underground train.
Medium: as Bjorn prepares to leave, he takes the brass key from its fixed place, looks back at Astrid and places it in her palm.
Wide: Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar step into the hall. Astrid closes the door from inside.
Insert from the hallway: the lock turns behind them while Carrie finishes the last of her coffee.

dialogueInline.text: I need one stamp on one paper.
Far enough that we take the train.
Keep the key with the room.

title: A Road With No Sky
summary: At the subway entrance Gunnar confronts the actual problem: the city expects travelers to surrender the sky and descend anyway.
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie starts down the station stairs without ceremony while Bjorn and Gunnar stop at the top.
Medium: Gunnar looks from the open sky behind him to the fluorescent stairwell below.
Wide: ordinary commuters pass around them and descend without hesitation. Carrie is already several steps down, coffee and folder in hand, waiting only long enough to confirm they are following.
Two-shot: Bjorn looks down the stairwell, then at Gunnar.
Wide: the two men finally follow Carrie underground.

dialogueInline.text: Now you want me to go where I cannot see it.

title: The Gate
summary: The fare gate produces one brief physical collision with the new system; Carrie gets them through without turning it into a lesson.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie taps a small transit card on the reader; the gate releases and she goes through.
Medium: Gunnar holds his card against the wrong part of the reader. Nothing happens. Carrie points once to the correct spot without stopping to explain the mechanism.
Close: Gunnar watches one commuter tap the correct spot without slowing.
Medium: Gunnar copies the physical action and the gate opens.
Wide: Bjorn follows after watching once; all three are through.

title: The Iron Worm
summary: The first train arrives as an enormous physical event; Gunnar confronts the machine while Bjorn immediately wants to know who is responsible for commanding something this dangerous.
panelPlan: Wide: headlight glare appears in the tunnel before the train itself. Wind pushes along the platform; Carrie automatically tucks the DTI folder tight against her body.
Large panel: the train roars into the station, metal, sparks, brake noise and reflected fluorescent light filling the space.
Medium: Bjorn sets his stance instinctively. Gunnar tracks the doors and wheels with intense attention. Carrie finishes the last of her coffee.
Medium: as the train stops, Bjorn looks along the length of it for the person visibly directing the operation; all he sees are doors opening and commuters moving.
Three-shot: Carrie bins or crushes the empty coffee cup and steps through the doors, turning back once to make sure the two men follow.

dialogueInline.text: The crew is in the cab.

title: Inside
summary: Inside, Gunnar loses the orientation he fought to recover while Bjorn investigates the equally strange social fact that the passengers organize themselves without a visible steward.
panelPlan: Wide: the doors close with the three inside a crowded car. Carrie wedges the folder safely between herself and the wall without losing track of either man.
Medium: the train accelerates into darkness. Gunnar looks through the window and gets only tunnel wall and reflected passengers.
Close: Gunnar braces through a curve, trying to feel direction through motion.
Medium: Bjorn watches riders make room at the doors, trade pole space and reposition for exits without anyone visibly directing them.
Medium: Bjorn asks an ordinary commuter who is responsible for where people stand; Carrie listens while shifting the folder to her other arm.

Wide: the car settles into its ordinary rhythm. Gunnar remains physically disoriented; Bjorn watches the crowd solve itself; Carrie has already begun looking like the only person in the group doing two jobs at once.

dialogueInline.text: I know where the train is going. I don't track every curve.
Who tells everyone where to stand?
Nobody. Move when the doors open.

title: No Horizon
summary: Gunnar discovers that north is not enough when every external reference has vanished; beside him, Bjorn keeps watching a crowd that somehow functions without visible command.
panelPlan: Medium: Gunnar watches station lights flick past in the tunnel.
Close: he looks upward as if the ceiling itself is an offense.
Two-shot Carrie/Gunnar: Carrie can tell him when they will get off, but not how the hidden route relates to the world above.
Medium: Bjorn watches riders begin gathering near the doors before the stop, apparently from memory rather than instruction.
Wide: the train continues through darkness; Gunnar gives up reconstructing every turn while Bjorn remains suspicious of a system that depends on everyone already knowing their part.

dialogueInline.text: Our stop is useful. Two more.
That tells me when to leave. Not where I am.
They are moving before the doors open.
So everyone is responsible for remembering for himself.

title: The Singer
summary: A busker gives Bjorn and Gunnar something underground that is immediately legible: a performer, an audience and voluntary payment.
panelPlan: Medium: a busker performs briefly in the car or at the platform edge during a stop.
Close: Bjorn listens with full seriousness.
Medium: Carrie puts a dollar into the busker's container.
Two-shot: Bjorn watches the exchange and contributes a small coin or bill Carrie gives him for that purpose.
Close: Gunnar listens as the train noise returns.

title: The Office Moves
summary: DTI changes Carrie's destination while they are already underground; Bjorn immediately notices that the supposedly chaotic train has kept its course more reliably than the bureaucracy that sent them onto it.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie's phone rings. She answers with the train moving behind her, pinning the folder under one arm to free a hand.
Medium: the supervisor tells her the appointment is now at the temporary annex.
Close: Carrie closes her eyes for one beat, then looks up sharply as the train slows at a station.
Three-shot: she ends the call, puts the phone away badly rather than neatly, and tells Bjorn and Gunnar they are getting off now.
Wide: the doors open. Carrie moves quickly; Bjorn follows while looking back down the train as it continues along the route it was already taking.

dialogueInline.text: Then you're halfway to somewhere else.
The train is still going where it was going.
The iron worm kept its route. Your office did not.

title: Ask Someone Who Knows
summary: At the transfer, Carrie solves the next piece by asking another rider; Bjorn notices that useful knowledge may be scattered among the people using the system rather than held by one visible commander.
panelPlan: Wide: the trio stands at a busy transfer junction with multiple stairs and platforms. Carrie's folder is now tucked under her arm at a slight angle rather than held neatly.
Medium: Carrie checks her phone, then the station information, then the movement of passengers.
Medium: she stops a passing commuter rather than pretending certainty.
Close: the commuter points toward a stair and gives one simple direction.
Wide: Carrie moves immediately. Bjorn watches the commuter disappear into the crowd before following; Gunnar follows Carrie. She does not stop to explain why asking worked.

dialogueInline.text: Down one level. Follow the green signs.

title: The Wrong Side of the Street
summary: They finally surface in an unfamiliar neighborhood; Gunnar can recover north from the daylight, but that does not tell any of them which building contains the moved DTI office.
panelPlan: Wide: the trio emerges into daylight among traffic, scaffolding and tall buildings. Carrie visibly relaxes for half a second at open air, then immediately pulls out her phone again.
Medium: Gunnar looks to the sky and fixes north using the sun and shadows now available.
Close: Carrie checks the destination while turning slowly at the corner; her hair and jacket are slightly less composed than they were at breakfast.
Two-shot: Gunnar gives her north; Carrie answers without looking up from the address.
Wide: they start walking, with Carrie leading.

dialogueInline.text: The city has many of those.

title: Eat Something
summary: The reroute consumes the morning, so Carrie forces a short food stop before continuing; the beat shows practical depletion rather than creating another financial-accounting exchange.
settingText: Street food cart near the temporary annex
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie stops at a street food cart because the reroute has consumed the morning. She is already opening the folder with one hand while ordering with the other.
Medium: the vendor hands over three simple lunches. Carrie takes hers and immediately steps aside to check the annex address again.
Medium: Bjorn watches Carrie eat standing up while still working; this is the first time all day he sees the cost of the errand on her rather than in money.
Medium: Gunnar watches the street while eating, still using people and physical movement rather than signs as his useful information.
Wide: Carrie finishes first, folds the wrapper into one hand, closes the folder and starts moving again before Bjorn and Gunnar have fully finished.

title: The Annex
summary: The temporary DTI annex is harder to identify than it should be; Gunnar contributes by watching where actual workers enter, not by reading modern signage.
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie stops at the correct street number, but the obvious public door is locked or inactive while temporary paper notices crowd the glass.
Medium: she studies the posted notices. For the first time all day she simply stands still for a beat, visibly tired of being redirected.
Medium: Bjorn watches a delivery worker disappear around the side of the building.
Close: Gunnar notices an employee with coffee use the same side entrance without hesitation.
Three-shot: Gunnar points to the people rather than the signs. Carrie looks once, accepts it immediately, and starts around the side without further investigation.

dialogueInline.text: Those people are going around the side.
Then we go around the side.

title: One Desk
summary: After the entire trip, the annex reduces to one plain desk and one clerk; Carrie handles the administrative details because that is her actual expertise.
panelPlan: Wide: plain municipal reception desk, stacked folders, chained pen, stamp pad. Carrie arrives with the once-neat folder now slightly bent from the trip.
Medium: she gives the clerk the paper and asks for the exact confirmation she needs with the automatic precision of someone finally back inside her own expertise.
Close: the clerk checks the file and reaches for the stamp.
Medium: Bjorn and Gunnar watch the physical object that the whole trip has been for. Carrie leans one forearm on the counter while she waits.
Insert: the rubber stamp comes down on the paper.

dialogueInline.text: Housing confirmation. I need the receiving stamp.

title: The Paper Changes
summary: The errand ends in seconds; Bjorn compares the tiny administrative act with the far more complicated transport system that actually delivered them there.
panelPlan: Insert: the fresh stamp on the document.
Medium: Carrie checks it once, closes the folder, and lets her shoulders drop for the first time all day.
Two-shot: Gunnar looks at the mark, then at Bjorn.
Medium: Bjorn gives his assessment of the journey. Carrie looks at him with no energy left to argue.
Wide: the three walk back toward the exit as another case replaces them at the desk; Carrie is already heading toward the subway again.

dialogueInline.text: The paper looks almost the same.
The iron worm moved hundreds of people with no steward in sight.
We crossed the city so one woman could strike this paper.

title: Back Under
summary: Carrie turns directly back toward the subway; the second descent is physically easier for Bjorn and Gunnar, but no one mistakes familiarity with the entrance for understanding the system.
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie leaves the annex and turns directly toward the nearest subway entrance without proposing a break.
Medium: Gunnar looks at the open sky one last time before descending again. Bjorn asks whether the same underground road returns them home; Carrie keeps walking.
Quick sequence: at fare control Carrie taps through; Gunnar and Bjorn repeat the physical action they learned that morning without comment.
Wide: Carrie leads them through the return transfer. By the time they reach the final train toward Bushwick, she finally gets a seat.

title: The Questions Begin
summary: Now that the return trip feels survivable, Bjorn and Gunnar finally have enough spare attention to become curious; Carrie's energy is already gone, and she lets the first wave of questions pass unanswered.
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie sits with the closed DTI folder on her lap, staring ahead. Bjorn and Gunnar stand nearby, no longer braced for immediate danger; for the first time underground they have room to wonder.
Medium: Gunnar studies the tunnel wall sliding past and wonders aloud how many men it took to dig a road this long beneath the city. Carrie does not answer.
Medium: Bjorn studies the metal car, rails and fittings and wonders aloud where anyone could have obtained so much iron.
Close on Bjorn as another question follows immediately: what sort of horses draw the train, and whether they mind living underground.
Close on Carrie. Same flat stare. She gives no indication that any answer is coming.

dialogueInline.text: How many men did it take to dig a road this long under the city?
Where did they get this much iron?
Do the horses that pull it mind living underground?

title: Not Question-and-Answer Time
summary: The questions expand from tunnels and iron into bureaucracy and the apparently incurious people around them until Carrie finally uses the first silence to set a boundary; Bjorn recognizes it immediately.
panelPlan: Wide: the train continues. Bjorn and Gunnar are now fully curious, talking past Carrie's silence rather than asking her directly.
Quick alternating panels: Gunnar wonders why the meeting moved; Bjorn wonders why the paper could not have been stamped at the first place; Gunnar wonders who had authority to move it.
Widen to the full car: Bjorn wonders where everyone is going and whether they all live nearby. Commuters sit, stand, read, sleep and stare at phones with complete indifference.
Medium: Bjorn asks why nobody seems surprised by any of this. Gunnar wonders whether all the passengers are also traveling somewhere to have papers stamped.
Hold one full silent beat after the last question. Carrie does not change expression.
Close on Carrie: she finally speaks. Bjorn recognizes the boundary immediately, begins an Astrid story, thinks better of extending the conversation, and accepts it.

dialogueInline.text: Why did they move the meeting?
If the stamp was all they needed, why could they not stamp it at the first place?
Who decided the meeting should move?
Where are all these people going?
Why does no one look surprised by anything?
Are they all going somewhere for stamps?
Ha! This I recognize. When Astrid was young I—

title: The Other Stair
summary: The train releases them through a different Bushwick exit; after recognizing Carrie's boundary, Bjorn and Gunnar do not ask her to solve the new uncertainty.
settingText: Bushwick subway station and unfamiliar exit
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie leads them up a staircase they did not use that morning, moving slowly now with the closed folder tucked under one arm.
Medium: Bjorn notices the change before they reach daylight but does not ask Carrie about it.
Wide: they emerge on the opposite side of the avenue from the entrance they remember. Carrie stops and simply waits.
Medium: Gunnar immediately looks for open sky and physical landmarks while Bjorn scans the block. Carrie says nothing.

dialogueInline.text: That is not the same place.

title: North Is Not Home
summary: Gunnar recovers north immediately above ground, but north alone does not locate 5B; Bjorn and Gunnar continue solving the problem themselves while Carrie conserves what little energy she has left.
settingText: Bushwick street outside alternate subway exit
panelPlan: Wide: traffic and buildings initially make the block look unfamiliar. Carrie remains a few steps behind rather than taking over.
Close: Gunnar checks the afternoon sky and fixes north.
Medium: he turns slowly, looking for something actually known rather than pretending direction alone solves the neighborhood.
Two-shot: Bjorn waits with him. Neither asks Carrie.

title: The Bodega
summary: Home becomes legible through repeated neighborhood experience: Bjorn and Gunnar recognize the bodega, orient from it, and take over the final walk without asking Carrie for anything.
panelPlan: Wide: Gunnar catches sight of the familiar bodega awning or window across the avenue.
Medium: Bjorn recognizes the entrance where he offered hacksilver.
Three-shot: the entire block resolves around that known point. Carrie sees that they have recognized it before she has to tell them.
Close: Carrie's shoulders loosen slightly. Bjorn and Gunnar start toward 5B; Carrie simply follows.
Wide: for the first time all day, Carrie is not leading the group.

dialogueInline.text: Then the room is that way.
I know one thing that is here.

title: They Lead
summary: The last blocks home are deliberately quiet: Bjorn and Gunnar carry the route while Carrie follows, making their recognition of her exhaustion behavioral rather than verbal.
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn and Gunnar walk ahead at an ordinary pace toward the apartment building; Carrie follows several steps behind with the folder tucked under her arm.
Medium: Gunnar checks the next corner against the bodega behind them and chooses the familiar direction.
Medium: Bjorn notices Carrie lagging, slows the pace slightly, and says nothing.
Close: Carrie notices the adjustment but does not acknowledge it aloud.
Wide: the three continue toward 5B in silence. Do not insert financial, transit or explanatory dialogue.

title: The Door Opens
summary: The trio reaches 5B without Carrie having to direct the final leg; the household opens the door from inside, and Carrie's workday visibly runs out of momentum at the threshold.
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn and Gunnar reach the familiar final stair first. Carrie comes behind them, one hand briefly on the rail, folder tucked against her side.
Medium: Bjorn knocks once rather than reaching for a key he does not have.
Medium: Astrid opens the door from inside with the brass key in hand; the Kin are visible behind her continuing ordinary household activity.
Wide: Bjorn and Gunnar cross back into the functioning room. Carrie enters last and sets the stamped folder down immediately.

dialogueInline.text: The road was longer than promised.
Most of it had no sky.

title: No More Questions
summary: Back in 5B, Carrie finally stops managing the day; Bjorn's recognition of her limit continues in silence while Gunnar returns to the open sky.
panelPlan: Wide: the household resumes around dinner. Carrie sits at the edge of the room with both hands around a glass of water; the stamped DTI folder lies closed nearby.
Medium: Gunnar starts toward Carrie with the alert expression of someone who has thought of another question.
Two-shot: Bjorn catches Gunnar's eye and gives one small head shake. Gunnar changes course without speaking.
Medium: Carrie sees none of this or chooses not to react; for once nobody needs anything from her.
Wide: Gunnar goes to the window instead. Bjorn rejoins the household.

title: What Gunnar Knows
summary: The issue closes on a modest, visual gain: Gunnar still does not understand the subway, but north, the bodega and 5B now connect one small piece of New York into something he can recognize.
panelPlan: Medium: Gunnar stands at the window with open sky visible again.
Close: he locates north without effort now that he can see the sky.
Medium from Gunnar's viewpoint: the familiar bodega corner is visible through the urban gap below.
Wide interior: Gunnar looks from that known point back into 5B. Carrie remains seated with her water; Bjorn and the household continue ordinary evening activity.
Final quiet panel: Gunnar leaves the window and rejoins the room. No one assesses what he learned, and no modern system is treated as mastered.

title: Next: The Neighborhood
summary: Editorial closing splash: the city is still enormous and mostly unreadable, but one block now contains repeated faces, repeated places and the beginnings of recognition.
panelPlan: Full-page closing teaser built around one ordinary Bushwick block at dawn: apartment stoops, storefront shutters lifting, the bodega, a coffee cart beginning service, and the route back toward 5B.
Bjorn may appear as a small figure on the sidewalk. The hook is not navigation mastery but repetition beginning to form local familiarity.
Use awnings, pale sky and sidewalk negative space for captions.
Do not show later Issue 5 payoffs such as remembered orders, established laundry routines or developed neighbor relationships.

dialogueInline.text: The subway is still a mystery.
dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION

dialogueInline.text: The block is becoming less mysterious.
dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION

dialogueInline.text: Tomorrow, some of the faces will be the same too.
dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION

directionInline: Closing teaser only. Preserve Issue 5 discovery and relationship development.
